El vértice es «lo mejor posible», y por: The vertex is “the best possible”, and that is why this is the first optimisation any student learns. With a fixed length of fence, the rectangle of maximum area is the square, and it comes from the vertex of a parabola; with a fixed advertising budget, so does the maximum profit. The path of any projectile is a parabola and its vertex is the maximum height: it is the calculation artillery makes, and also the one a basketball player makes without knowing it.

La parábola no está sola: es una de las: The parabola is not alone: it is one of the four conics, the curves you get by cutting a cone with a plane. They are in [[ge-conicas|conics]], and there the parabola stops being “the graph of $x^2$” and becomes what it really is: the locus of points equidistant from a point and a line.

Que un proyectil describe una parábola l: That a projectile describes a parabola was proved by Galileo around 1638, and it was far more subversive than it looks: it contradicted Aristotle's physics, according to which the projectile went straight until its impulse ran out and then fell like a stone. Galileo understood that the motion splits into two independent ones, a uniform horizontal and an accelerated vertical, and that combining them gives a parabola. It is the first time a mathematical curve described a real physical phenomenon.

¿De dónde sale $-\\frac{b}{2a}$? De la s: Where does $-\frac{b}{2a}$ come from? From symmetry: if there are two roots, the vertex is exactly halfway between them, and the midpoint of $\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{\Delta}}{2a}$ is $\frac{-b}{2a}$ because the roots cancel.
